items.description: R1 (#625): "NodeMemoryStalled (critical) and NodeMemoryStallElevated (warning) have both been firing on srvk8s3 since ~2026-08-13, across 485 five-minute buckets." / "Alertmanager still has no receiver configured, so none of it was sent anywhere." / "Two coupled facets: the alert rules trust a counter that can wedge, and there is no delivery path to notice when they misfire — or when they fire for real." Both facets are closed on production: the two stall alerts no longer fire on a wedged counter alone (today they read the stall rate and nothing else — HelmCharts configs/prd/prometheus/prd/values.yaml:75-97), and Alertmanager, on the chart's stock receiver with no configuration today (values.yaml:120-130 sets none), delivers alerts to Telegram.

items.area: R2 — Grafana and pgAdmin on Keycloak (#575)
items.description: R2 (#575): "Put Grafana and pgAdmin behind the homelab Keycloak (`homelab` realm at https://auth.ginbov.nl/realms/homelab) instead of their app-local logins, same shape as dnsmasq / electronics-inventory / iot / guacamole / open-webui / zigbee2mqtt already use" — per-app confidential client, secret in OpenBao at eso/<cluster>/<app>/<stage>/oidc, materialised by ESO, OIDC config in the chart/release values (the dnsmasq shape: HelmCharts configs/prd/dnsmasq/prd/values.yaml:19-51). Holds for production's Grafana and pgAdmin (ruling D6), with their secrets at eso/prd/grafana/prd/oidc and eso/prd/pgadmin/prd/oidc; no client secret appears in any committed file.

R3: "a Keycloak upgrade would be warrented" — Keycloak is built at 26.7.3 in DockerImages (26.5.1 today, keycloak/build-matrix.json:5), every charts/keycloak release is pinned to it (HelmCharts charts/keycloak/values.yaml:22 pins 26.5.1 today) and both production Keycloak stages, auth.ginbov.nl and keycloak-dev.home, run it, with a backup of Keycloak's database taken before the push that deploys it, and that backup's keycloak_prd_db dump kept outside the postgres-pas backup scope's count-based pruning (the newest 90 objects — HelmCharts configs/prd/postgres-pas/_shared/infrastructure.tf:72-73) until 26.7.3 is verified working. The dev-cluster release's deploy waits on srvk8sdev (fact F3).

Each stall alert fires only when available memory is low or major faults are high as well: NodeMemoryStalled and NodeMemoryStallElevated additionally require, on the same node, MemAvailable under 10% of MemTotal or major page faults above 500/s, with their stall thresholds (0.05 / 0.02), severities and for-windows otherwise unchanged (HelmCharts configs/prd/prometheus/prd/values.yaml:75-97 today). The 2026-08-02 incident meets both signals (0.62 GiB MemAvailable, 670–770 major faults/s — AnsibleSpecs handovers/memory-issues/06-eviction.md:73, 02-measurements.md:136).

A new warning-level alert fires when a node's memory stall rate is above 0.02 while MemAvailable is above 25% of MemTotal and major faults average under 50/s over an hour, held for at least an hour. Once firing it keeps firing through that node's memory dips and fault bursts for as long as the stall rate stays above 0.02, and resolves when the counter stops (a reboot). Its message names the node and says the stall alerts on that node are blind until it is rebooted.

The production alerting rules load and evaluate without errors. After deploy, neither stall alert fires on a production node whose stall counter is healthy, and the wedge warning fires only on a node whose counter is genuinely wedged — a wedge that happens during the run is the warning working, not a failure. The rules also evaluate cleanly while a node-exporter chart upgrade leaves two overlapping series per node that differ only in helm_sh_chart: checked against data while such an overlap is still within Prometheus's 7-day retention (HelmCharts configs/prd/prometheus/prd/values.yaml:3), and by reading the rules once it has aged out.

Production Alertmanager delivers to the chat of a new, dedicated Telegram bot (neither eso/prd/jenkins-telegram-bot nor eso/prd/telegram-mcp is reused): critical alerts delivered loud, warning alerts delivered silent, resolved notices sent, plain text. The bot token and chat id come from OpenBao eso/prd/prometheus/prd/telegram via ESO and appear in neither git nor the rendered Alertmanager configuration.

Delivery covers the production cluster's Alertmanager only: the dev cluster's Prometheus release is unchanged, no SMTP gateway or mail-derived event receivers are added, and Alertmanager gains no ingress.

On production, an account holding the grafana Keycloak client's admin role signs in to Grafana through Keycloak as Grafana Admin, and a homelab-realm account without that role — F1's friend — cannot log in.

On production, an account holding the pgadmin Keycloak client's admin role signs in to pgAdmin through Keycloak as a pgAdmin administrator that already lists and can connect to the chart's postgres-pas server (HelmCharts charts/pgadmin/files/servers.json), and a homelab-realm account without that role cannot log in.
Production's Grafana and pgAdmin each keep their local admin and login form as break-glass; Keycloak is an additional login button, with no automatic redirect.

items.area: D6 — dev-cluster copies keep local login
items.description: The dev-cluster copies of Grafana and pgAdmin keep their local login: the dev Grafana release is unchanged, and the dev pgAdmin release rendered from the changed chart shows no Keycloak login and references no OIDC secret.

items.area: D5 / U1 — Keycloak never runs beside an older version
items.description: Every Keycloak rollout stops the old pod before the new one starts (ruling D5; the chart surges a second pod today — HelmCharts charts/keycloak/templates/keycloak-deployment.yaml:10-14), so the rollout that deploys 26.7.3 never runs a 26.5.1 and a 26.7.3 pod against the same database at once (Keycloak upgrading guide, "Migrating to 26.6.0"), and keycloak-dev.home runs 26.7.3 healthily before auth.ginbov.nl does.

After the upgrade, the homelab and homelab-dev login pages render with the deployed themes; a sign-in through an app already on Keycloak succeeds on homelab, and a sign-in to the account console succeeds on homelab-dev (no production-cluster app uses that realm).

items.area: D2 — stall alerts inhibited on a wedged node
items.description: While the wedge warning fires for a node, Alertmanager inhibits that node's NodeMemoryStalled and NodeMemoryStallElevated, so neither is delivered from a wedged node, including through a memory dip or fault burst on that node long enough to meet the stall alert's for-window; stall alerts on other nodes and every other alert are not inhibited. The inhibition matches on the node label, which every production series of node_pressure_memory_stalled_seconds_total carries (Prometheus series API, 2026-09-14).
